post.caption: Aluminum once belonged in a jewelry store. In 1854 Henri Sainte-Claire Deville announced a way to make it, and Emperor Napoleon III funded the work. In 1855 Paris showed it off as silver from clay, and aluminum was priced like a precious metal. The emperor's baby son had an aluminum rattle set with diamonds. The Cooper Hewitt holds an aluminum and gold bracelet from around 1860. In 1884 Tiffany's displayed the aluminum tip of the Washington Monument. In 1886 Hall and Héroult each found a cheaper way. Both were 22 years old.
